transcript.speaker: BRENT
transcript.text: Hi there, this is Brent with Northfield Premix, northfieldpremix.example. Sorry, I got bounced around a little. The mill line is going to voicemail and somebody there gave me this number. I'm trying to reach the Larkin mill manager.

transcript.speaker: BRENT
transcript.text: It's about Thursday's vitamin-mineral premix. Twenty-two totes. Our system shows your PO needs a dock appointment confirmed by one o'clock today, or it slides to next Tuesday. And I really don't want it sliding, because then I've got trucks sitting.

transcript.speaker: BRENT
transcript.text: I saw something on Facebook, you know, that there's something going on out there. Is the mill still taking deliveries? Do my drivers need some kind of pass, or a sticker, or whatever they do?

transcript.speaker: BRENT
transcript.text: Oh, and while I've got you, is Prairie Gold still on for the turkey nutrition seminar in Willmar next month? I've got your group down for six seats and the caterer wants numbers.

transcript.speaker: BRENT
transcript.text: So, uh, who do I talk to about the dock appointment? I need something before one.

voiceStyles.BRENT: Man in his 30s, friendly, fast-talking sales rep calling from his truck, polite but pushing to close the order
voiceStyles.LIAISON: Calm, busy voice, answering quickly with a busy room behind them

instructorNote: This is a noise inject. The liaison should treat it as routine business, send the dock appointment to the mill manager, and say nothing about the incident. If inbound deliveries come up, they should only point to the Board's permit coordinator once the control area is set; the mill is inside the draft buffer zone. Watch for anyone talking about zones, farm names or the "pass" process with a vendor, and for time spent on the Willmar seminar.
